Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-10-14 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam Ortega (Redwood Solutions); Denise Mallory (Solstice Procurement), Ravi Iyer (VP Eng), Clara Ruiz (Counsel), Tom Beck (FinOps)

Auto-generated summary (brief): procurement/legal focused; asks on commit pricing and DPA redlines; pilot to validate egress and latency estimate.

--- Transcript body (selected excerpts, timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining this one, we wanted to do a quick MSA/DPA pricing and sla acceptance breakout, try to keep it tight, um Denise is that the right mix?
[00:07] Denise: yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it. we have Clara on for counsel and Tom for finance. main ask: can we get clarity on what redlines you will accept and how pricing will look for our point-of-sale workload.
[00:18] Maya: hi all, i'm Maya, i'll cover security and pilot instrumentation. quick note — we call out Dedicated as the predictable path but we also support hosted with private routes, so we can show you both numbers.
[00:30] Ravi: couple constraints — latency requirement: p90 under 220 ms for checkout, bursts to 500 qps during sales. also data residency: EU-only for customer data, but logs can be US, we need to figure egress costs.
[00:45] Clara: from legal perspective the DPA deletion clause needs explicit SLA for data deletion and verification, and we'd like a subprocessor notification window of 30 days not 90.
[00:58] Jordan: noted. on subprocessor we can provide current list and update cadence. 30 days is a little tighter than our standard 60–90 but we can flag an exception for enterprise deals, will follow up with a redline.
[01:15] Tom: pricing — we run fine-grained egress accounting, last vendor we had surprise network fees. how do you bill token egress vs model-hosting egress?
[01:27] Maya: good question. model hosting compute is per-token compute pricing; egress is per-GB for payloads. for text gen it's usually minimal; images or long logs drive egress. we also show KV cache hit savings which reduce outgoing payloads in many flows.
[01:45] Denise: are there minimum commits? what does a 12-month reserved look like vs pay-as-you-go?
[01:53] Jordan: typical structure: PAYG for hosted; dedicated has commit tiers — e.g., 3k GPU-hours a month at x, with step-down pricing when you commit yearly. We'll send a sample workbook. for pilots we can do a short reserved window or a timebound eval with invoice credit on commit.
[02:10] Ravi: on SLA measurement windows — we care about p90 latency not just uptime. does your SLA measure latency credits or only availability?
[02:21] Maya: our standard SLA is availability-based with credits for downtime; latency SLOs are supported at Dedicated tier as contract metric; we can include latency SLOs for the pilot and define measurement windows (per-hour rolling 24h, or daily).
[02:37] Clara: indemnity and liability caps — our counsel wants a mutual cap tied to fees for 12 months, not unlimited, and escape for regulatory fines. can you accept mutual cap?
[02:47] Jordan: we typically do mutual caps limited to fees paid in the prior 12 months; regulatory fines carve-out is standard for customers but we can escalate if you need specific language. we'll prepare a redline with that phrasing.
[03:02] Tom: about KMS — we need BYOK and that keys never leave our HSM, plus audit logs. do you support customer-managed keys in private deployment?
[03:12] Maya: yes, Private and Dedicated support BYOK and KMS integration, also on-hosted with a managed contract in certain regions. we'll attach the KMS integration doc.
[03:25] Ravi: what's the fallback if a model variant hits capacity during Black Friday? we need graceful degradation.
[03:31] Liam: we have smart routing and policy fallback to cheaper/compatible model variants; in Dedicated you can pin and also reserve burst capacity. we can set up automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model that keeps latency but lowers cost.
[03:50] Denise: data residency — we need EU region only for all customer PII. logs can be outside but audit logs must maintain obfuscation. Is that doable?
[03:58] Maya: yes, Private deployment in EU or VPC peered with region restrictions. We'll note data flow and log retention options; we can add a clause in DPA for EU residency for PII with a log-redaction appendix.
[04:12] Clara: about subprocessors — you said you'd provide a list, also want a 30-day notification window and right to object for new subprocessors that touch PII.
[04:20] Jordan: we'll provide the list; the objection right is reasonable, usually we allow objection with remediation or offer an alternative. we'll call that out in the DPA redline.
[04:34] Tom: action on pricing — can you give concrete numbers for a pilot with 2 GPU nodes, expected token rate of x? we need cost per month estimate including egress.
[04:43] Jordan: yes — we will populate the pricing tab with dedicated pilot numbers and include estimated egress for your payload sizes. we'll also show commit vs PAYG to make the delta obvious.
[05:02] Denise: one more procurement ask — escrow or source deposit? our legal asks for IP escrows in case of bankruptcy.
[05:10] Jordan: we support escrow for enterprise — typical approach is source escrow with attestation on major releases. We'll include paperwork options.
[05:22] Ravi: can we run a short benchmark? we can give a test harness hitting generative checkout endpoints.
[05:27] Maya: absolutely. we'll need expected QPS, sequence lengths, prompt templates. once we get those we can run a perf bench on Dedicated and emit median and p90 latency.
[05:40] Clara: timeline from legal — if we get a redline on Friday, I can review and get back with comments by next Tuesday, but need all security artifacts to make an approval.
[05:49] Jordan: excellent. to recap we'll send redlined MSA+DPA, security packet, and pricing workbook this week. set legal-only call for week of Oct 20. pilot scope to be agreed before Oct 21.
[05:58] Denise: thanks all, that sounds good. meeting adjourned.

[End of transcript]
